resolvedFindings.criterion: Round-2 case (c) / spec v5 requirement 'A spawn_worker for an issue at todo writes in_progress (the first phase worker starts the work)' and its three document statements
resolvedFindings.evidence: On the real daemon a child released at todo is admitted as its own tree: reduceIssueUpdated (reducers.ts:904) emits admit for any issue reaching todo; admit() -> ensureTree(child) -> startRoot -> spawnTree writes in_progress for tree.root (processes.ts:2360), which is the child. Rig: LEGSMOKE-98 released via /waves/release at 06:25:25 -> state.trees[LEGSMOKE-98] active gen 1 with its own root pane @3 %3 and boot-token file, admission slot taken, daemon PATCH in_progress at 06:25:27.409 (event 3840) with no spawn involved; the parent's /worker/spawn {tree: LEGSMOKE-97, issue: LEGSMOKE-98, role: planner} -> 500 'Issue LEGSMOKE-98 does not belong to Legion tree LEGSMOKE-97' (spawnWorker entry check, processes.ts:544). Live deployment (read-only GET /legion/v1/state on 127.0.0.1:13370) matches: every released child is its own tree (LEGION-21/22/23/54/56 active or lingering; LEGION-24/25/31 queued at todo, promoted by their own spawnTree). Therefore the trigger documented at workers.ts:66 ('The first worker on a child released at todo'), packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md /worker/spawn row ('the first phase worker on a child released by waves/release'), skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md step 6 item 2 ('when you spawn_worker the first worker for a child released at todo'), and spec v5's 'a child issue released at todo stays at todo until its implementer finishes' does not exist; the unit test 'writes in_progress when the architect spawns the first worker for a child released at todo' pins a state the daemon never reaches (child at todo with no trees[child], spawned from the parent's tree). The reviewer's round-1 premise (children never sit at in_progress) was wrong. The branch itself is reachable and correct only when a human moves an already-active issue back to todo (admit() no-op for an active tree): proven as (c') on LEGSMOKE-97 -> exactly one PATCH in_progress after the spawn. Daemon behaviour is right either way; the docs and spec describe a path that is not there. Architect decides: reword the trigger to the reachable case or drop the todo branch and its test; fix the spec bullet.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Fixed at 5005733c (spec v6): the todo branch and its test removed; a spawn at todo now writes nothing (new test api.test.ts:2289); the three passages say every released issue, root or child, gets in_progress at admission and the spawn-time write exists for the corrective round alone. The round-2 rig case (c) result stands as the proof that the daemon never reaches a released child at todo without in_progress already written by its own admission; the round-2 (c-prime) write on an active issue moved back to todo is the behaviour the spec now rejects and the new unit test pins its absence.
